correctness.rationale: Deleting all leaves on the large side of a spanning tree of \(K_{d,m}\) leaves a finite core with at most \(d-1\) retained large-side vertices because \(\sum(\deg(v)-1)=d-1\). Re-expanding a fixed core is exactly a weak composition of \(m-k_F\) among the \(d\) small-side vertices, modulo the core automorphism action. The action on that side is faithful because two distinct retained large-side vertices with the same neighborhood would create a 4-cycle. Burnside therefore gives the displayed root-of-unity rational generating function, hence a quasipolynomial of degree \(d-1\) and period dividing \(\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,d)\). The reciprocal-automorphism sum combined with the labeled-core count yields the stated leading coefficient. The assigned verifier independently reconstructs all cores for \(d\le4\), compares literal orbits with Burnside counts, and matches the known small-\(d\) formulas and tables.
